title: Cloud IDS Security Alert Event (Objective 2 evidence contract)
description: Frozen cross-layer contract between the Phase 1 detection layer and the Phase 2 evidence-logging layer. The detection layer of record is the Phase 1 LightGBM multiclass detector: 25 NetFlow features, seven coarse threat categories, isotonic-calibrated confidence, trained and evaluated on NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018-v2 (18,893,708 flows; https://staff.itee.uq.edu.au/marius/NIDS_datasets/). Field order below is normative for canonical serialisation of the Phase 2 envelope; see docs/canonicalisation_spec.md. Version 2.0.0 supersedes 1.0.0, which described a different detector (a PyTorch binary classifier on CICIoT2023) and therefore admitted threat categories the deployed detector cannot emit and recorded calibration as absent when it is in fact fitted.

contract_version.description: Version of this frozen alert contract. A consumer must reject any event whose contract_version it does not recognise rather than guess at field semantics.

event_id.description: Globally unique identifier for this detection event, assigned once by the detection agent at emission time and never reused. Carried through unchanged from the Phase 1 alert.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of the detection event, millisecond precision, as emitted by Phase 1.

verdict.description: Binary verdict. Translated from Phase 1's ANOMALY/NORMAL vocabulary; ATTACK if and only if threat_category is not 'Benign'.

threat_category.description: One of the seven coarse threat categories the Phase 1 detector is trained to emit, collapsed from the fifteen fine-grained NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018-v2 Attack values by Phase_1/config.py:ATTACK_MAP. This enum is exactly Phase 1's label space: Phase 2 does not admit categories the deployed detector cannot produce, and does not carry an 'Other' escape hatch, because a multiclass detector that cannot resolve a category is a detection result to investigate, not a value to place on-chain.

severity.description: Operational severity, carried through from Phase 1's severity map (Phase_1/outputs/10_contract/severity_map.json) and renamed to this vocabulary. It is NOT re-derived from calibrated_confidence: Phase 1 rates Infiltration 'critical' despite its low mean confidence (0.303) because a missed post-compromise intrusion costs more than a missed flood, and a confidence-derived severity would silently overturn that decision.

calibrated_confidence.description: Calibrated P(attack) in [0,1], as emitted by Phase 1. This is the probability of the attack class, not the probability of the argmax category. Objective 3's anchoring gate is a threshold on this value, so its interpretation as a probability depends on the calibration block below.

calibration.description: Calibration provenance for calibrated_confidence, so an auditor can distinguish a calibrated probability from a raw model score without inspecting the producer.

is_calibrated.description: True when the emitting detection layer fitted a calibrator. True for the Phase 1 detector, which fits isotonic regression on the validation fold.

method.description: Calibration method applied, or 'none' if calibrated_confidence is a raw model score. 'isotonic' for the Phase 1 detector.

expected_calibration_error.description: Measured ECE on the held-out test fold, as reported by Phase 1 stage 08. Present when the producer measured it; this is the evidence that the anchoring gate may be read as a probability threshold.

source_address.description: Source IP or IP:port, carried as nullable alert metadata only. Phase 1 deliberately excludes identifiers from the feature space (destination port alone can reach 70-100% accuracy on these datasets); they travel here so an analyst can act on an alert without the model having trained on them.

destination_address.description: Destination IP or IP:port, nullable metadata only, for the same reason as source_address.

resource_id.description: Cloud resource identifier that observed the flow. Phase 1 derives this deterministically from the destination host because NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018-v2 carries no asset inventory; in deployment it is replaced by a cloud inventory lookup. Documented, not hidden.

triggering_features.description: The feature vector consumed by the model for this flow, keyed by feature name, so an auditor can recompute the verdict independently of the live model service. Stored off-chain; the on-chain record commits to it via detection_contract.feature_digest.

model_id.description: Stable logical identifier for the deployed model family. For the Phase 1 detector this is the model_id_sha256 recorded in its model card, which covers the booster, the ordered feature list, the label order and the hyperparameters.

model_digest.description: SHA-256 over every prediction-affecting component of the deployed artifact (serialised model, feature ordering, label ordering, hyperparameters, per-class thresholds). See src/model_provenance.py. Anchored on-chain once per retraining cycle (contracts/model_provenance.schema.json) and referenced by every alert produced under that model.

version_label.description: Human-readable version label as emitted by the producer, e.g. 'flat_tuned_tau-fa8d2667cc39'.

feature_attributions.description: Ranked per-feature attributions for this verdict (SHAP values from Phase 1 stage 10), most influential first. May be empty when the producer did not compute attributions for this event.

contribution.description: Signed contribution toward the predicted class.

detection_contract.description: The producer's own frozen-contract digests, carried into Phase 2 and independently verified there. Phase 1's CONTRACT.md designates event_hash as the value committed on-chain, so it travels with the event rather than being replaced by Phase 2's envelope digest. Two digests with distinct scopes therefore coexist by design: event_hash (producer, pipe-joined canonical string, Phase_1/outputs/10_contract/CONTRACT.md) and payload_digest (consumer, canonical JSON, docs/canonicalisation_spec.md).

producer.description: Which component emitted the alert, e.g. 'Phase_1/10_alert_contract.py'. A synthetic load generator must identify itself here so generated events are never mistaken for measured detections.

schema_version.description: Version of the producer's own alert contract (Phase 1 freezes 1.0.0).

event_hash.description: The producer's SHA-256 over its canonical string, recomputed and checked by Phase 2 via src/phase1_contract.py before the event is admitted. This is the value anchored on-chain.

feature_digest.description: The producer's digest over the feature vector alone, letting the on-chain record commit to the features without carrying them.

anchor_gate_tau.description: The calibrated confidence gate in force when the producer made its anchoring decision. Phase 1 selects tau to meet an Integrity Coverage Ratio target (0.9997655 for ICR 0.9568 at 11.43% on-chain volume).

producer_anchor_decision.description: The producer's own anchor flag. Phase 2 preserves this decision rather than re-deriving it from a rounded confidence, so the two layers cannot disagree about which events were selected.

digest_verified_by_consumer.description: True when Phase 2 recomputed and confirmed event_hash and feature_digest from the payload. Recorded explicitly so an auditor can tell verified evidence from merely transported evidence.

payload_digest.description: SHA-256 of this event's canonical JSON serialisation (docs/canonicalisation_spec.md), computed over every field except payload_digest itself, and reproduced byte-identically by chaincode/securitylog/canonical.go. This is the digest of the Phase 2 evidence envelope, independently recomputable by an auditor.

inference_latency_ms.description: Measured wall-clock inference latency in milliseconds for this single flow, as reported by the producer.
